info.name: Crumb & Co. — Admin Only
info.description:
Admin-only flows for the Crumb & Co. e-commerce backend (Express v5 + Prisma).

## Setup
1. Start the server: `npm run dev` (defaults to http://localhost:4000).
2. Seed the database: `npm run db:seed` (creates the admin `admin@crumbco.dev` / `Admin123!`, products).
3. Import the environment `crumb-and-co.environment.json` and select it.

## How to run
- Run the whole collection in order (Auth . Users . Products → Orders → Negative Tests).
- The first request (Login Admin) captures the JWT in the environment variable `adminAccessToken`; every admin-only request reads it via `Authorization: Bearer {{adminAccessToken}}`.
- Self-contained: the admin creates its own product and manages its own managed user. Order-status tests reuse an existing order captured from the all-orders list (orders are created by customers).
- Re-running is tolerant: create requests accept 201 (first run) or 409 (already exists); ids are recaptured from list endpoints.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Admin login, plus a second user used by the user-management tests. The admin token is stored to `adminAccessToken`.

item.name: Login Admin
item.description: Uses the seeded admin (see `npm run db:seed`). Stores the JWT in `adminAccessToken`, used by every admin request in this collection.

item.name: Register Managed User
item.description: Second account targeted by the user-management tests. On re-runs this 409s (already registered) — the id is captured reliably by the following Login Managed User request.

exec: pm.test('201 on first run (409 if already registered)', () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Login Managed User
item.description: Always returns the managed user's id (even on re-runs when registration 409s), so `managedUserId` is reliably set for the Users folder.

item.name: Users (Admin)
item.description: Admin-only user management. Requires `adminAccessToken` (set by Auth > Login Admin).

item.description: Admins see all orders and can transition status. The order id is captured from the all-orders list — run the Customer collection first if there are no orders yet.
